title: Informal lessons and Bunk falling asleep at the Caravan rehearsal
summary: Lessons became talk; Bunk fell asleep holding his horn with an iron grip while Blumberg and Mielke tried to rehearse for the Caravan job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Uh, did he ever, uh, to get back to that one detail of counting, did he ever talk, insist on you stomping your foot all the time, or did he say anything about that much?

I know some pupils he had. No, there, there was just the one time when he said, this is the way you, you know, you're gonna, you're gonna play lead, you know, and, and you got to stomp off the tunes, and, uh, you know, and this is the way you, you beat your foot, you know. Mm-hmm. And, uh, he was trying to tell me how to run a band. Well, at the time I wasn't interested in learning how to run a band. I was interested in finding out what made him tick. Yeah. I mean, he was the guy that fascinated me, and I, and I guess I was less interested in taking lessons than in, and talking to him. Mm-hmm. And, uh, uh, trying to figure him out, you know. And, uh, sometimes I'd come up there, and he'd fall asleep on me, you know. Yeah. I mean, he'd be a drowsy, the apartment would be overheated. Yeah, that's happened to me. Yeah. Yeah. Plenty of people, yeah. He was the most relaxed. And he'd be sitting in an easy chair, and, and I'll never forget Bob Milkey and I went up once, and, and, uh, I guess Bunk was really sleepy. And he, uh, he was, uh, lying across the bed, and, and, uh, I don't know if he'd been drinking the night before or something, but, but, you know, we were supposed to come up and have some kind of rehearsal for, oh, that's right. It was for this, uh, this series of jobs we played with Bunk. And, and so we got up there, and he was lying across the bed, and he, he got, got up and got his horn out, I think. But he was so sleepy, he could just hardly keep his eyes open. And the next thing we knew, he had, he had suggested a couple tunes that we ought to do. I think, uh, he wanted to do, uh, Beale Street Blue.

Oh, you were talking about this rehearsal you were going to have? Yeah, the rehearsal for the Caravan. Was it the Caravan? Yeah, Mustard Van. Yeah. And we went up there, it was just Bob Mielke and myself, to talk over tunes we were going to do. And we were talking about Beale Street Blues, and Bunk sang a couple of the themes and got his horn out and played a few notes, I guess. And the next thing we knew, he was all sound asleep, and so we didn't know just what to do. We were kind of standing there, and so we tried to put his horn away for him, because he's lying there on the bed with the horn on his chest, and his hand just kind of draped over the horn lightly, bent at the wrist. And so we tried to get his horn out of his hand, and it was like a grip of iron. You know, you couldn't get the horn, you wouldn't let go of the horn, you know, and yet he was snoring away. And we were trying to get his fingers off the horn, and he just had to give up finally. It was like glue, you know. And I guess it's an old habit to hold on to your horn, all circumstances. But, so we just had to leave him there with the horn, and there were times he'd fall asleep when I was talking to him. There was one time when I visited him, he was staying at the Loughborough's apartment downtown in New York. I don't have any idea what the order of these different residences was.
It was probably later than the Freddie Moore, I think, anyway. I may have that documented someplace, too. But anyway...
